## Applicability / Aplicabilidade

This is a **Git repository** — the backup strategy is Git itself.

## Backup Mechanism / Mecanismo de Backup
<!-- source: .git/, GitHub remote -->

| Aspect | Current State | Evidence |
|--------|--------------|----------|
| Primary storage | GitHub (cloud) | git remote -v |
| Local copies | Developer machines | git clone |
| Backup frequency | Every `git push` | Real-time with each push |
| History retention | Full history (19 commits) | git log |
| Distributed copies | 2+ (GitHub + local machines) | Git is distributed by design |

## RPO / RTO

| Metric | Value | Notes |
|--------|-------|-------|
| **RPO** (Recovery Point Objective) | Last git push | Uncommitted changes are at risk |
| **RTO** (Recovery Time Objective) | < 5 minutes | `git clone` from GitHub |

## Disaster Scenarios / Cenários de Desastre

### GitHub goes down
- **Impact**: Cannot push/pull, but local copies work
- **Mitigation**: All code exists on developer machines
- **Recovery**: Push to alternative remote (GitLab, BitBucket)

### Local machine failure
- **Impact**: Uncommitted changes lost
- **Mitigation**: Push frequently, commit small changes
- **Recovery**: `git clone` from GitHub

### Repository deletion (accidental)
- **Impact**: Total loss if no local copies
- **Mitigation**: Keep local clones on multiple machines
- **Recovery**: GitHub support can restore within 90 days

## Failover / Failover

**[NOT DETECTED]** — No secondary remote configured.

**Recommendation**: Add secondary remote (BitBucket or GitLab) for redundancy:
```bash
git remote add backup https://bitbucket.org/user/repo.git
git push backup main
```
